prompt: Create ONE single image, 4:3 aspect ratio: a 2x2 grid of 4 SEPARATE illustrations (2 columns, 2 rows) for a children's picture book, all panels exactly the same size and perfectly aligned, plain white gutters between and around the panels, no frames, no captions, no text, letters or numbers anywhere. Style: Children's picture-book illustration, soft watercolor and gouache with gentle pencil lines, warm golden light, earthy Middle-Eastern palette (sand, olive green, terracotta, sky blue), rounded friendly faces with expressive eyes, ancient Near-East setting of the Torah era: tents, desert hills, stone villages, simple wool and linen robes, head coverings, sandals. Calm, warm, safe mood. HEAD COVERING RULE for every panel: every man and every boy (including sons, shepherds, servants, neighbors and children) ALWAYS has his head covered, never bare: a kippah (skullcap) in modern or sages-era scenes, a tallit worn over the head, or in ancient scenes the hood or corner of his robe/cloak drawn over his head or a head-cloth tied with a cord. This overrides any mention of hair in a character description (the hair may show beneath the covering). Women and girls keep their head scarves or coverings as described. Keep every character exactly the same in every panel where they appear: Moshe: Very old man of about 120, slender and slightly stooped, long flowing white beard and white hair, kind tired brown eyes with smile lines, warm olive skin, simple light cream linen robe with a sand-colored sash, plain undyed head cloth, leather sandals, always holds a tall plain wooden shepherd's staff. No glow or rays around his head; Batya: Little girl about 5 years old, small and round-cheeked, light brown skin, thick black curly hair tied back with a red cloth band, big curious dark eyes, long-sleeved soft red-orange wool dress reaching her ankles, barefoot or small sandals; signature item: a red hair band; Eli: Boy about 6 years old, skinny and lively, tan skin, short messy dark brown hair, very big round brown eyes, gap-toothed grin, short-sleeved sky-blue linen tunic with a rope belt, sandals; signature item: a little rope belt with a knot hanging at the side; Savta Tzipora: Batya's grandmother, about 50, plump and warm, olive skin, gentle laugh lines, grey-streaked dark hair fully covered by a long olive-green head cloth, long modest terracotta robe, a woven striped shawl over her shoulders; signature item: the striped shawl. Panels in reading order: 1 BOOK COVER: Old Moshe sits on a large flat rock beside the Jordan River at golden late afternoon, staff resting across his knees, telling a story with one hand raised. Batya and Eli sit cross-legged at his feet looking up in wonder, Savta Tzipora behind them, and a soft crowd of families blurs into the background. Beyond the river, gentle green hills glow. Medium-wide shot, warm and inviting, Moshe and the children as the clear focus. 2 Wide establishing shot of a sandy desert plain beside the winding Jordan River in soft morning light. Old Moshe sits alone on a big smooth boulder near the water, staff in hand, looking peacefully across the river. Tents of the camp stand in rows behind him, reeds and a few palm trees line the bank. Calm, quiet, spacious composition with Moshe small but clearly in focus. 3 Excited children run across the sand toward Moshe, Eli in front with arms waving and mouth open calling, Batya right behind him. Families follow from the tents: fathers and mothers, grandparents with walking sticks, babies carried in arms, Savta Tzipora among them smiling. Moshe on his rock, waiting kindly. Dynamic diagonal composition, dust kicked up gently, bright morning. 4 Moshe, seated on his rock, speaks with a far-away look while the children listen. Above them, inside a soft swirl of golden sand like a dreamy memory, a long line of people walks out of a land of great stone buildings and palm trees toward an open desert at dawn, carrying bundles and leading goats. The memory is pale and gentle, the listeners in the foreground warm and clear.
